run_metadata.coverage_summary: This run was again constrained by the environment's network egress policy: every direct page fetch (WebFetch) to tender portals and buyer websites failed at the proxy with DNS/egress errors (ENOTFOUND), including all Tier 1 government portals (AusTender and the 8 state/territory eTendering sites), VendorPanel, buy.nsw, tenders.vic and data.gov.au. Only WebSearch (which routes through Anthropic infrastructure, not the egress proxy) was available, and it is US-indexed so it reflects buyer portals imperfectly and with a lag. Within that limit the run did two useful things. (1) Opportunity discovery: WebSearch surfaced several buyer-originated procurements that discovery-signal aggregators list as currently active; three were corroborated enough to record at headline level (NSW Police Stage 2 CPS/CDAS, Sydney Metro Commercial Advisory Services Panel, Victoria Police prescription safety eyewear). Because no detail page could be opened and the specific closing dates traced back to aggregators (not the buyer notice), closing dates and IDs that could not be verified were left null and the reported values noted. All three are counted in entries_pending_detail. (2) Source discovery: three genuinely new buyer-originated sources were identified with real URLs (CBH Group e-tender portal, Ports Victoria procurement, Victoria Police Annual Procurement Plan). Tier 3 was checked (SAP Ariba/Business Network Discovery, BHP GCMS+Ariba, Fortescue Ariba, CBH) and found registration/invitation-gated; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed, so none were fabricated.
gaps: CRITICAL: WebFetch outbound egress is fully blocked by the environment's network policy. Every attempted fetch returned a DNS failure (ENOTFOUND), including www.tenders.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au. No tender portal, detail page, or specification document could be retrieved. This is the same constraint that produced 0 tenders on 2026-10-05 through 2026-10-10.

Tier 1 government portals (AusTender + all 8 state/territory eTendering sites) could not be queried live; buy.nsw and tenders.vic are JavaScript-rendered so WebSearch returned only partial/stale snippets of their open-tender lists.

Detail/deliverables/requirements/evaluation-criteria extraction was impossible this run (detail pages and tender documents are only reachable via WebFetch, which is blocked). The three recorded tenders are headline-level only.

Closing dates and tender IDs for the recorded tenders could NOT be verified against the buyer's own notice. Specific dates surfaced by WebSearch traced back to discovery-signal aggregators (australiantenders.com.au), which must not be treated as source of truth; those dates were therefore left null in the date fields and reported in notes as unverified.

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP (GCMS + SAP Ariba), Fortescue (SAP Ariba Network), Rio Tinto and CBH expose opportunities only behind free supplier registration or invitation; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed. Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope by definition.

Leads seen via search but NOT corroborated as currently open, so deliberately not recorded as tenders: Brisbane City Council November items (Botanic Gardens river access, Walter Taylor Bridge scaffold, ex-TC Alfred sports-field remediation pkg 3, traffic signal hardware) — a targeted follow-up could only confirm Aug 2026 closings and BCC's move to SAP Ariba; Fraser Coast Regional Council water-reservoir roof replacements (reported closing 11 Nov 2026); DEECA property cleaning (reported 10 Dec 2026); Ports Victoria Station Pier fender upgrade (reported 30 Nov 2026); South Gippsland Water Riflebutts Rd SPS (reported 17 Nov 2026); NSW Premier's Department Facilities Management (could not corroborate — likely a mismatch); CFA Cann Valley Fire Station alterations (could not corroborate).
WebSearch is US-indexed and does not reliably reflect the live state of Australian tender portals, so even the source-discovery and opportunity results may lag the portals.
recommended_seed_additions: Whitelist the Tier 1 tender domains (tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au/buy.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au, supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, tenders.act.gov.au) and vendorpanel.com.au in the environment's network egress policy — without WebFetch access the routine cannot detail or verify tenders.
CBH Group e-tender portal (cbh.com.au/suppliers/e-tender-portal) — WA grain-handling co-operative; buyer-originated corporate e-tender channel.
Ports Victoria procurement (ports.vic.gov.au) — Victorian port GBE publishing a FY26-FY27 procurement activity plan; open tenders listed on Buying for Victoria; contact procurement@ports.vic.gov.au.
Victoria Police Annual Procurement Plan (police.vic.gov.au/annual-procurement-plan) — buyer-originated forward procurement plan / market-sounding signal.

Buyer reference pattern (YR-2026-...) is consistent with current NSW Police procurements.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only. WebFetch egress is blocked, so the buy.nsw detail page could not be opened and no deliverables/requirements could be extracted. The closing date reported by the discovery-signal source (~20 Oct 2026) could not be verified against the live notice and is therefore left null. tender_id is taken from the aggregator reference and should be reconfirmed on buy.nsw.

discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for Australian resource/agribusiness supplier portals surfaced CBH Group's dedicated 'E-Tender Portal' on its own suppliers site while searching mining/resources buyers.
discovered_sources.notes: CBH Group is a large WA grain-handling and marketing co-operative. Buyer-originated corporate e-tender channel; individual opportunities are behind portal registration. Could not be fetched this run (egress blocked); existence confirmed via search result only.

discovered_sources.source_name: Ports Victoria — Procurement / Procurement Activity Plan

discovered_sources.notes: Victorian port corporation (GBE). Publishes a forward procurement activity plan on its own site and lists open tenders on Buying for Victoria; procurement contact procurement@ports.vic.gov.au. Buyer-originated. Plan PDF not fetchable this run (egress blocked).

discovered_sources.how_discovered: WebSearch for Victoria Police procurement surfaced the force's own 'Annual Procurement Plan' page listing planned sourcing activity; it complements the opportunities Victoria Police publishes on Buying for Victoria.
discovered_sources.notes: Buyer-originated forward procurement plan (market-sounding / discovery signal) for a major Victorian buyer. Use to anticipate upcoming RFx, then pivot to tenders.vic for the live notice. Not fetchable this run (egress blocked).
